topic: Domino's 30-minutes-or-free guarantee was dropped in 1993 after a huge court verdict over a crash involving a delivery driver
title: Domino's Promised 30 Minutes. A Court Verdict Ended It.

draft_script: Domino's had a legendary marketing promise: 30 minutes or your pizza was free. It sounded like a great deal. For years, this guarantee fueled their growth. It made Domino's famous for speed. But this promise put extreme pressure on drivers. Every delivery was a race against the clock. Drivers pushed limits. The guarantee incentivized speed above all else. It was a business trick that risked safety. Then, in 1993, a Domino's delivery driver crashed. The accident was severe. A woman suffered serious injuries. She sued Domino's. Her argument: the 30-minute guarantee forced reckless driving. It created a dangerous system. A jury agreed. They found Domino's responsible. The court verdict was massive. Domino's paid millions in damages. This legal blow changed everything. Immediately after the verdict, Domino's dropped their iconic 30-minutes-or-free guarantee. A marketing promise designed to win customers instead cost them millions. It was a loophole that backfired. A true business trick gone wrong.
